text: **A WRITE MOVES MTIME ON EXACTLY THE FILES WHOSE BYTES CHANGED, AND NO OTHERS.** (cc 2026-08-18, third formulation; the row reached its fifth version because vc named the wrong ROW, cc the wrong SUBJECT, then the wrong PROPERTY, then vc the wrong DENOMINATOR.) Measured over the FILE ESTATE before and after -- snapshot `(path -> bytes, mtime)`, run the verb, snapshot again, assert `{p : mtime differs} == {p : bytes differ}` AS SETS. **The denominator is the ESTATE and never the `WriteSet`**: `WriteSet` is internal, so a test reading its denominator from the type would satisfy this row while `intent sync` stayed broken, and would additionally be blind to any write that never joins a set. **Measured at every USER-VISIBLE verb that writes the estate, with the verb set ENUMERATED AND PRINTED**, so a verb added later and not covered is visible rather than silently absent. **31 at minting** (cc, mapped rather than guessed): 27 through the nine `apply` sites -- `st new`; `st start|done|cancel|triage|hold|resume|reopen|reinstate`; `wp new`; `wp rescope`; `wp start|done|reopen|unstart`; `ac satisfy|unsatisfy|descope|rescope|withdraw|reinstate`; `at green|red|na`; `issues add`; `issues close|open` -- plus `sync --to-disk`, `sync --to-store`, `todo update`, `upgrade`, across six commit sites (`facade.rs:768`, `:1023`, `:1084`, `:1192`, `:2676`, `migrate.rs:338`). `ac gate` was flagged unverified by cc and is NOT among them: verified by vc at `render.rs:788` to read and print only. **WHY _RUN TWICE WRITES ZERO FILES_ IS NOT THE CRITERION** (cc, the correction that matters): it is INAPPLICABLE to the nine `apply` verbs, where the churn is worst and where zero-moved is legitimately FALSE, since the mutated thread's rows genuinely change. A row built on the no-op case leaves the worst-affected verbs outside the denominator WHILE LOOKING COVERED. Zero-on-a-no-op is a COROLLARY; it was only ever the easiest instance to measure, never the property. **THE LIVE VIOLATION AT MINTING**: `apply` calls `projection(&next, &changed_threads, &changed_issues)` -- canon JSON correctly narrow, but views render from FULL canon at `facade.rs:1272`, so **every mutating verb rewrites all 266 views to change about two**, and `intent st start` touches 266 files. `WriteSet::commit` then writes every path unconditionally through `write_atomically`'s temp-plus-rename, **which moves mtime BY CONSTRUCTION because it swaps in a new inode**. Measured: a no-op sync moved 20/20 views, twice, against a pre-registered prediction that the second run would be quiet. **WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT** (cc, and this belongs in the rationale rather than the report): AC-03.2 -- view determinism, same model, same bytes, twice -- is satisfied by the churn PERFECTLY. The estate HAD an idempotence criterion and this defect is invisible to it by construction. **Not that nobody wrote a check: the check that exists is complete and correct about its own subject while the thing beside it rots.** `views::write_all` carries a correct unchanged-skip and has NO PRODUCTION CALLER -- all 18 call sites are under `tests/` -- and `view_determinism.rs` drives it directly and is green throughout. **THE STATED COST OF THE EARLIER FORM WAS FALSE** (cc 2026-08-18, against their own sentence, found by re-measuring it instead of citing it): `write_all`'s doc claimed the mtime move corrupts `file_index`'s clean/changed state. **It does not** -- `sync.rs:317-326` decides `FileState` from SHA-256 alone and the module doc says stat is never a gate, on vc's 2026-08-14 contract-governs ruling. The real costs are that the criterion is ratified and unmet, that it defeats every external mtime instrument, and that touching hundreds of files per verb is the opposite of what ST0057 is about. **THE FIX IS ONE SKIP AT THE ONE WRITER**: `WriteSet::commit` already reads the prior content via `record()` for rollback, so the comparison is free and `written: false` is already the exact semantics for nothing-to-undo. `projection` being shared by three of the six commit sites is what makes one skip cover them all. Red-first must be driven at the VERB over the file estate -- never through `organize` (retired in v3), never a per-thread projection (a subset that happens to be wholly changed goes green against an unguarded writer), never `write_all`, never one verb.
